title: Check Point Scales Its SASE Platform on Microsoft Azure for Global Enterprise Deployment
body_markdown:
[Check Point Software Technologies Ltd.](https://www.checkpoint.com/) (NASDAQ: CHKP), a pioneer and global leader in cyber security solutions, today announced an expansion of its collaboration with Microsoft to deploy[Check Point SASE](https://www.checkpoint.com/harmony/sase/) on Microsoft Azure. The collaboration will enable enterprises to scale secure access across global environments with greater performance, resilience, and centralized control, while advancing Zero Trust, AI adoption, and identity-driven security.


As organizations consolidate networking and security through SASE, and as distributed workforces and AI-driven traffic push more demand to the edge, the underlying cloud infrastructure has become critical to delivering consistent connectivity, policy enforcement, and user experience at enterprise scale. By building on Microsoft Azure, Check Point is extending the cloud foundation of Check Point SASE to support larger deployments, broader geographic reach, and more flexible traffic routing across the SASE mesh.


The expansion builds on Check Point’s broader collaboration with Microsoft across enterprise and AI security. A member of the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program and a member of the Microsoft Intelligent Security Association, Check Point recently became a Solutions Partner with certified software. Earlier this year, Check Point announced an upcoming integration with Microsoft Copilot Studio to help organizations securely build and deploy generative AI agents with embedded protection, governance, compliance, and threat prevention.


“Enterprise SASE deployments are becoming larger, more distributed, and increasingly performance-sensitive,” said Amit Bareket, Vice President of Cloud & SASE Customer Experience at Check Point Software Technologies. “Expanding our collaboration with Microsoft allows us to better support complex global environments, from large user populations to high-throughput sites, while maintaining the centralized management and prevention-first security customers expect from Check Point.”


“As enterprises modernize secure access for distributed users and applications, cloud infrastructure and identity are critical to delivering consistent performance and protection at scale,” said Anne Sheehan, Vice President, Enterprise Partner Sales, EMEA at Microsoft. “Our relationship with Check Point helps customers extend secure access across global environments, combining Microsoft Azure’s trusted cloud platform with Check Point’s prevention-first security to support Zero Trust, protect sensitive data, and enable confident AI adoption.”


The expanded deployment of Check Point SASE on Microsoft Azure is expected to provide:


- An expanded Check Point SASE footprint supported by 48 additional Microsoft Azure Points of Presence (PoPs)
- Identity-centric Zero Trust architecture through integration with Microsoft Entra
- Use of the Microsoft global network, with direct interconnection to more than 4,000 internet partners, to support the Check Point SASE deployment Optimized, location-aware routing to Microsoft 365 and Azure, with administrator control over entry and exit points across the SASE mesh
- Integrated AI security to discover, govern, and protect AI applications, agents, and AI-driven workflows across the enterprise
- Access to the Check Point SASE platform, including Check Point Private Access, Check Point Internet Access, and Check Point SaaS Security


Check Point SASE delivers industry-leading threat prevention, achieving a 99.8% malware block rate in[Miercom’s 2026 Hybrid Mesh Network Security Competitive Assessment](https://engage.checkpoint.com/2026-miercom-hybrid-mesh-network-security-benchmark/items/report--miercom-hybrid-mesh-network-security-competitive-assessment-2026) . It also delivered the fastest average secure browsing speed among the solutions tested, reaching 1.13 Gbps. With hybrid secure internet access, users connect directly to the internet while critical protections remain enforced on the device.


**Availability**
Check Point SASE is expected to become available through Microsoft Marketplace in the first half of 2027, simplifying procurement, accelerating deployment, and enabling enterprises to maximize their existing Microsoft cloud investments.


Customers interested in the new SASE infrastructure should contact their Check Point representative to discuss early availability, onboarding timelines, and deployment options.
